title: What's your preferred way to handle environment secrets in local dev?
body:
I've tried `.env`, direnv, 1Password CLI, and just exporting things in my shell config. Curious what everyone lands on for a daily driver — especially when juggling five projects at once.

Bonus points if it plays nicely with Docker Compose and doesn't leak into git by accident.

comments.body: direnv + 1Password CLI is the combo that finally stuck for me. Each project gets a `.envrc` with `op run --env-file` and the secrets never hit disk as plaintext.

replies.body: Seconded. The `op run` wrapper is the killer feature — you get the secret injected into the subprocess only.
Does that work with VSCode's debugger? I remember hitting friction there.
You have to launch VSCode from inside the direnv shell — the debugger inherits the env. Not elegant but works.
Has anyone measured the startup cost? direnv adds a bit of latency to every `cd`.

comments.body: Honestly I just use a `secrets.local.json` file that's gitignored, and a tiny `make` target that exports it. Zero tooling, works everywhere, and I never accidentally commit it because it's in `.gitignore` from the start.

replies.body: This is what I'm running now. My concern is: what stops a collaborator from accidentally copying their production values into the local file?
A README warning and code review, which I admit is fragile. But so is every solution here.

comments.body: We use HashiCorp Vault in prod but for local dev we generate short-lived credentials on `make dev`. Zero persistent secrets on laptops. Would recommend if you already have Vault.
